results.title: Ghana risks industrial stagnation if research fails to reach industry – Zanetor
results.content: Environment, Science and Technology Minister Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings has warned that Ghana risks industrial stagnation if universities and research institutions fail to translate scientific discoveries into practical solutions for businesses and industry. She said the disconnect between academic research and commercial application was limiting the country’s ability to turn scientific knowledge into industrial growth, job creation and economic development. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings was speaking at the opening of the 2026 Oliver Reginald (O.R.) Tambo Chairs Initiative (ORTARChI) Conference at the West African Genetic Medicine Centre (WAGMC), University of Ghana, Legon.

results.title: How many lawyers does Ghana need?
results.content: Seeing people you once taught put on their wigs and gowns brings a special satisfaction. You remember their questions, their struggles, and their determination. Their achievement becomes part of your reward for teaching. Around this time, a familiar question returns to the public space: “Are we producing too many lawyers?” It is a fair question. What is curious is how readily we offer answers without establishing the context or examining the data. Too many lawyers for which roles, in which locations, and measured against what demand? results.title: Obuasi SHTS scandal will not fade from public attention – Education Minister
results.content: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has vowed that the sexual abuse allegations at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) will not be allowed to fade from public attention without a resolution. Speaking at a press conference in Accra on Monday, October 26, 2026, the Minister said the case would not follow the pattern of other major public controversies that attract intense media attention before gradually disappearing from the national conversation. “Amid the calls from various sections of society for a full-scale investigation of similar malpractices in other educational institutions in the country, this scandal won't suffer the same fate as other burning issues which are normal to be discussed with gusto in the media over a period and then go out with a whimper. That won't happen in respect of this matter,” he said.

results.title: Ghana climate portal targets young Africans with learning tools for climate action
results.content: The Ghana Climate Literacy Portal (GCLP) is seeking to equip more young Africans with the knowledge and resources needed to respond to climate change, as youth advocates gather in Accra to discuss practical solutions to the continent’s environmental challenges. The digital learning platform is drawing attention at the Regional Conference of Youth Africa (RCOY Africa), where young climate advocates are exploring ways to strengthen youth participation in climate policy and develop recommendations for decision-makers. Saustine Lusanzu, a Tanzanian climate advocate and founder of the Earth Care Foundation, said access to reliable climate learning materials could help young people move beyond awareness and take practical action in their communities.
